title: Reading the Unspoken
note: He defines this as knowing what a ruler has in mind without being told. It comes here because no one who serves rulers can do without it.

couplets.plain: Someone who can look and know what is meant, with nothing said, is an ornament to the world of unfailing waters.
couplets.pm: The minister who can tell from a ruler’s face and eyes what he intends, so that he doesn’t have to say it, is an ornament to the people of the world, which unfailing water surrounds. His clear mind adorns everyone.

links.quote: look and know what is meant, with nothing said

couplets.plain: Hold anyone who knows without doubt what is in another’s heart as equal to a god.
couplets.pm: Someone who can know for certain what goes on in another’s mind may be only human, but hold him in honour as equal to a god. He doesn’t match a god in body and the like, but he has the divine power of knowing what others think.

links.quote: knows without doubt what is in another’s heart
links.reason: Rates certainty about another’s heart so high that its owner is held the equal of a god.

couplets.plain: To gain those who can read a thought from its signs, give any of your limbs.
couplets.pm: Those who know how their own thoughts arise, and so can read the thoughts of others, are worth any of the parts of the realm they ask for. Rulers should give it and take them as helpers. The inner working is the same in everyone, so your own mind is the tool. The parts are outer things: wealth, land, elephants, horses and the like.
couplets.note: The Tamil can go two ways on the sign: he takes the first sign to be your own thought, others, like the plain reading, the other person’s. உறுப்பு is a limb. He takes it as the outer parts of a realm.

links.quote: gain those who can read a thought from its signs
links.reason: Says those who can read a thought from its signs are worth having at any cost.

links.remove: The council is the old English. The Tamil names no ruler and no council.

couplets.plain: Those who grasp a thought unspoken match other people limb for limb, yet they are different.
couplets.pm: Those who can’t grasp what someone has in mind without being told may be like those who can in body, but they differ in understanding. He says “different” because, lacking the highest understanding, such people are beasts.

links.quote: Those who grasp a thought unspoken

couplets.plain: If eyes can’t read a thought from its signs, what use are they among the body’s parts?
couplets.pm: If the eyes, which can see what is shown to them, can’t read the thoughts of others, what else do they do, these finest parts of the body? He gives the eyes the soul’s power of knowing because they help it most in reading signs. Such eyes are of no use.

links.quote: eyes can’t read a thought from its signs
links.reason: Holds that eyes unable to read a thought have no use among the parts of the body.

links.quote: what use are they among the body’s parts

couplets.plain: As crystal shows what lies beside it, the face shows what is strongest in the heart.
couplets.pm: Crystal takes on the colour of whatever is beside it and shows it. In the same way a person’s face takes on and shows what is uppermost in the heart.

links.quote: the face shows what is strongest in the heart

couplets.plain: Is there anything wiser than the face? In gladness or in anger, it gets there first.
couplets.pm: Nothing knows more than the face. When the soul turns to gladness or anger towards someone, the face knows and gets there first. To those who say only the soul knows, and a face made of the five elements can’t, he answers that it blooms in gladness and darkens in anger. So the face is the means of reading thought.

links.quote: In gladness or in anger, it gets there first

couplets.plain: If you have someone who can look within and know what has happened to you, it is enough to stand and look at their face.
couplets.pm: Someone in need who finds those who can read his mind from signs and end his trouble need only stand and look at their faces as they look at his. To go past that and speak would shame both of them, so there is no need. The face is the means of reading.

links.quote: look within and know what has happened to you
links.reason: With someone who can read your heart, you need say nothing: standing before them is enough.

couplets.plain: The eyes themselves will tell enmity and friendship, if you have those who know the ways of the eye.
couplets.pm: If rulers have ministers who can tell one kind of look from another, the eyes of foreign rulers will tell the enmity or friendship in those rulers’ hearts, though they say nothing. The kinds of look are the look of dislike and the look of delight.

links.quote: The eyes themselves will tell enmity and friendship
links.reason: For those who know its ways, the eye alone tells enmity from friendship.

couplets.plain: Look into it, and those who call themselves subtle have no measuring rod but the eye.
couplets.pm: Ministers who think their understanding subtle have, on inquiry, only their eyes as the rod to measure a ruler’s mind. Gesture, form, action, speech and many other measures exist, but a person who knows of them can hide them. A look mingles with the mind and can’t be hidden, so he names it alone.

links.quote: no measuring rod but the eye
